After crossing the railroad tracks the corridor would proceed diagonally to the northeast. The diagonal alignment will leave triangular pieces of land to be developed which could result in poor local street patterns and inefficient use of land. Between the railroad tracks and 6th Street the area is zoned light industry with the corridor traversing an auto salvage yard and airport clearance zone lands.
East of 6th Street the corridor would be in close proximity to the airport's taxiway and holding apron area adjacent to Runway 7R. In the past the adjacent residential area was subjected to a very high level of noise from nearby aircraft activities. However, Milwaukee County has implemented their Master Plan for Air Terminal expansion by acquiring the entire neighborhood for the development of their 60 acre Air Cargo Area. The relocation of buildings and site clearance has been completed.
With these recent land acquisitions and the fact that this corridor lies within the limits of the new air cargo facilities this corridor will be in conflict with future airport expansion plans.
The corridor would cross Howell Avenue just south of Grange Avenue and north of the existing Howell Avenue tunnel before sweeping sharply to the north of the airport entrance road. The corridor would be west of the existing corporate aircraft hangars.
The Federal Aviation Administration and airport officials have reviewed this corridor and were concerned that its straight alignment, and its parallel alignment to Runway 7R may be misleading to landing aircraft.
